lots.what_it_is: Japanese four-drawer tansu, a narrow tall single-case chest in plain softwood (probably sugi) with a dark worn finish, iron lock plates with keyholes and forged iron swing handles on each drawer, iron carrying rings on the sides, early 20th century (Meiji to Taisho style). The title's 'TANSY' is a misspelling of tansu.
lots.condition: Heavy honest wear: scuffed and abraded fronts, rusty but complete iron fittings, paper label remnants with brush script on the drawer fronts and a pasted paper strip with brush writing down the back. Drawers open and the interiors look sound in photo 6. Top edge has some splits and losses (photo 2). Keys not mentioned.
lots.key_photo_findings: All six originals re-checked on the contact sheet. Iron lock plate with keyhole and a round boss, swing bail handles, iron side rings, pale softwood drawer sides. Paper label on a drawer front reads as brush characters (one looks like 田 above another character), and the back strip is brushed script: these are inventory or ownership labels, not a maker's mark. No maker, seal or date found. Form is narrow and tall (roughly one drawer wide), smaller than the Gowans comparables.

lots.what_it_is: Small carved pale stone corbel (cul-de-lampe or pendant bracket form) with deep undercut foliate carving and drilled holes, tapering to a moulded ringed stem, with a flat sawn back and a round fixing hole in one side. Stone looks like a fine pale limestone or very pale sandstone. Age and origin unproven: Gothic or Gothic Revival European, or a later garden or architectural copy are all possible.
lots.condition: Heavily weathered and pitted, leaf tips and ring edges worn or chipped, a hairline crack or seam on the front, orange iron staining on the back. Back is flat cut. No size given; it looks roughly 20 cm across.
lots.key_photo_findings: Five originals re-checked. Photo 2 and 3 show the flat sawn back with a round drilled hole (fixing or lifting hole). Photo 5 shows the moulded ringed stem and foliate bowl clearly. No mark, mason's mark or date seen. Background in photos 1 and 2 shows Chinese scroll paintings, so the consignment may include Asian pieces; a Chinese or garden origin cannot be ruled out. The wiring of the ticket hides part of the stem.
